A Unified Framework for Complex Systems

The Vision

We are witnessing convergence across disciplines suggesting universal principles govern all complex systems.

  • From cellular metabolism to global economics
  • From neural networks to social organizations
  • From ecosystems to technological infrastructure

Gradient-Coupled Systems Theory (GCST) proposes these systems share a common "operating system" based on gradient dissipation and capital formation.

2 / 10

The Core Innovation

Traditional View

Systems maximize immediate energy dissipation (Prigogine)

Individual structures optimize independently

GCST Innovation

Systems strategically invest in capital to enhance future dissipative capacity

Coupled systems create emergent collective behaviors

Dissipative Capital Formation (DCF) explains the emergence of complexity at all scales

3 / 10

Project Scope

Theoretical Development

  • Formalize mathematical framework for gradient coupling dynamics
  • Develop metrics for dissipative capital across domains
  • Create predictive models for system behavior

Practical Applications

  • Creordics: Decision-making framework grounded in physical law
  • Tools for organizational design and policy evaluation
  • Bridges to AI, climate science, economics, healthcare

Immediate Steps

  • Core team assembly: Identify key contributors (physics, complex systems, domain experts)
  • Literature synthesis: Map existing relevant work across disciplines
  • Working group formation: Establish communication channels and collaboration structure
  • Initial formalization: Draft mathematical framework for gradient coupling
  • Case study selection: Choose 2-3 domains for early validation
  • Funding strategy: Identify appropriate grant opportunities and institutional support

Acknowledging the Challenges

Scientific Challenges

  • Measuring coupling strength across heterogeneous systems
  • Quantifying "dissipative capital" in consistent units
  • Bridging vastly different time and space scales

Practical Challenges

  • Interdisciplinary communication barriers
  • Resistance from established paradigms
  • Complexity of real-world validation

These are features, not bugs—the difficulty reflects the framework's ambitious scope
